label: Data Movement: Unload Data
topic: Data Movement: unloading data with COPY INTO a location

questions.scenario: A Data Engineer runs COPY INTO @exports/daily/ FROM (SELECT ...) FILE_FORMAT = (TYPE = CSV COMPRESSION = GZIP) SINGLE = TRUE FILE_EXTENSION = 'csv.gz' MAX_FILE_SIZE = 1073741824. A downstream job expects exactly one file named report.csv.gz in that location. The unload succeeds, but the stage contains a single file named data, with no extension. The result set is about 600 MB before compression.

options.text: Add INCLUDE_QUERY_ID = TRUE so the file is named from the query ID, then rename it
Put the file name and extension in the path, as in @exports/daily/report.csv.gz, and keep the compression matching the extension
Remove FILE_EXTENSION and rely on COMPRESSION = GZIP to add .csv.gz
Raise MAX_FILE_SIZE to 5368709120 so Snowflake names the file from the file format

explanation.correct: With SINGLE = TRUE, Snowflake writes one file named data and ignores FILE_EXTENSION. The name and extension must be part of the path, and the compression should match the extension.

distractors.A: INCLUDE_QUERY_ID = TRUE is not allowed with SINGLE = TRUE, and it would add a UUID to the name anyway.
distractors.C: FILE_EXTENSION is already ignored with SINGLE = TRUE, so removing it changes nothing. The file still comes out as data.
distractors.D: MAX_FILE_SIZE only sets the target size per file, up to 5 GB. It does not affect the name, and 600 MB already fits in the current 1 GB value.

questions.scenario: A Data Engineer must unload the relational table customers, which has NUMBER and VARCHAR columns, as JSON to a stage. The statement COPY INTO @exports/customers/ FROM customers FILE_FORMAT = (TYPE = JSON) fails.
questions.stem: Which change makes the unload work?

options.text: Add HEADER = TRUE so that the column names become the keys of each JSON record
Set TYPE = AVRO, which writes each row as a JSON-like record with its column names
Add STRIP_OUTER_ARRAY = TRUE so that each row is written as one separate JSON document
Unload FROM (SELECT OBJECT_CONSTRUCT(*) FROM customers) with TYPE = JSON

explanation.correct: TYPE = JSON works only when unloading a VARIANT column. Wrapping each row with OBJECT_CONSTRUCT turns it into one, and the output is one JSON document per line.

distractors.A: HEADER writes column headings in CSV files. It does not make a relational table unloadable as JSON.
distractors.B: Avro is not supported for unload. The formats are CSV, JSON and Parquet.
distractors.C: TYPE = JSON works only for a VARIANT column, whatever other options are set.

questions.scenario: A nightly job runs COPY INTO @exports/orders/ FROM (SELECT ...) PARTITION BY (TO_VARCHAR(order_date)) OVERWRITE = TRUE and fails. The goal is one set of files for each order date.
questions.stem: What should the Data Engineer change?

options.text: Remove OVERWRITE = TRUE, because a partitioned unload cannot be combined with it
Set INCLUDE_QUERY_ID = FALSE, because the query ID in file names conflicts with PARTITION BY
Add SINGLE = TRUE so that each value of the partition expression is written to one file
Replace TO_VARCHAR(order_date) with an integer expression, because PARTITION BY needs a number

explanation.correct: PARTITION BY cannot be combined with OVERWRITE = TRUE, SINGLE = TRUE or INCLUDE_QUERY_ID = FALSE.

distractors.B: INCLUDE_QUERY_ID is forced to TRUE with PARTITION BY and cannot be set to FALSE.
distractors.C: SINGLE = TRUE cannot be combined with PARTITION BY.
distractors.D: The PARTITION BY expression must evaluate to a string. An integer expression is not accepted.

questions.scenario: A nightly unload writes files to a fixed path in a bucket. Snowflake occasionally retries the unload internally, and after those retries the path holds extra files from the earlier attempts.
questions.stem: Which option avoids the extra files?

options.text: Set OVERWRITE = TRUE so that every retry replaces all of the files that an earlier attempt wrote
Set SINGLE = TRUE so that the retry writes one file and cannot create extra files
Set INCLUDE_QUERY_ID = TRUE so that a retry removes the files that carry its query ID
Set DETAILED_OUTPUT = TRUE so that a retry lists the earlier files and skips writing them

explanation.correct: With INCLUDE_QUERY_ID = TRUE the file names carry the query ID, and a retry removes files with the current query ID before it rewrites them. It is recommended over OVERWRITE to avoid duplicates.

distractors.A: OVERWRITE replaces only files with the same name and does not remove other files, so retries may still leave extra files.
distractors.B: SINGLE = TRUE writes one file, but a retry can still leave a file behind from the earlier attempt.
distractors.D: DETAILED_OUTPUT changes only what the statement returns, one row per file. It does not change how files are written.

questions.scenario: A security team creates the AWS policy for a storage integration that the nightly unload job uses to write to s3://exports-bucket/daily/. The policy must grant only the object permissions that unloading needs on that path.
questions.stem: Which permissions should the policy grant?

options.text: s3:GetObject and s3:GetObjectVersion on the path
s3:PutObject on the path, and nothing else
s3:ListBucket and s3:GetBucketLocation on the bucket
s3:PutObject and s3:DeleteObject on the path

explanation.correct: Unloading to S3 needs s3:PutObject and s3:DeleteObject on the path.

distractors.A: These permissions let Snowflake read objects, which loading needs. They do not allow writing files.
distractors.B: s3:DeleteObject is also required for unloading, so PutObject alone is not enough.
distractors.C: These are bucket-level permissions and do not allow writing or deleting objects on the path.

questions.scenario: A team reviews how COPY INTO <location> behaves before it automates unloads. The jobs write to cloud storage paths, and some run against tables that can be empty or that have masked columns.
questions.stem: Which THREE statements are correct? (Select THREE.)

options.text: When the source has zero rows, no file is written to the location
GET can download files from a named external stage as well as from internal stages
Snowflake gives no warning when it unloads into a location that holds files
A single COPY INTO <location> can unload every table in a schema
NULL_IF on unload writes NULL as the last value in the NULL_IF list
Masking policies on the source columns apply, so a role may unload masked values

explanation.correct: A source with zero rows writes no file. There is no warning when the location is not empty, so use an empty path or INCLUDE_QUERY_ID = TRUE. Masking policies on source columns apply to the unload.

distractors.B: GET works on internal stages only. External stages are read with the cloud provider's tools.
distractors.D: One statement unloads one table or one query. A schema or database cannot be unloaded in one statement.
distractors.E: On unload, NULL becomes the first value in the NULL_IF list.
